page.helper.ctaSub: No install needed — video is already peer-to-peer in the browser.
page.helper.lead1: A small program for your computer. It runs a full mini-hub with the chat UI and a public HTTPS tunnel — an independent island people can open even if this seed site is down.
page.helper.lead2: It does not give you control of this website or admin tools. Stop anytime with Ctrl+C.
page.helper.osNote: macOS may ask to allow the binary under Privacy & Security the first time. Windows may show SmartScreen for an unsigned .exe — choose “More info → Run anyway” if you trust this site after verifying the checksum. Full Apple/Microsoft code-signing is optional and not required for open-source builds.
page.helper.step1d: Runs a mini match node on your machine and a free HTTPS tunnel so others can reach it. Video still goes browser-to-browser — not through you as a media server.
page.helper.step2code:
# Windows (PowerShell as user)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\rulet-helper.ps1

# macOS
chmod +x rulet-helper-mac.sh && ./rulet-helper-mac.sh

# Linux
chmod +x rulet-helper.sh && ./rulet-helper.sh
page.helper.step2d: First run downloads the bridge (+ cloudflared if needed) into ~/.ruletka-helper (or %USERPROFILE%\.ruletka-helper on Windows).
page.helper.step3d: The helper prints a public URL — open /live.html on it to chat on your hub even if the seed site is offline. Optional: email support@ruletka.vip if you want operators to consider federation into the shared stranger pool.

page.privacy.childrenBody: The Service is 18+ only. We do not knowingly allow minors to use it. Sexual content involving minors is strictly prohibited. If you believe a user is underage, use Report and stop the call. Age confirmation in the client is not a government ID check.

page.privacy.friends: Friend lists, friend requests, and blocks for this hub are stored on the server instance you connected to, so features like call-when-online and offline friend messages can work. Friend DMs may be stored on the hub until delivered or cleaned up. Match chats are primarily kept on your device after a call ends.
page.privacy.hubsBody:
• The product is designed so other people can run their own hubs. A third-party hub is a separate operator with its own logging and retention.
  • If you connect to a non–ruletka.vip hub, that operator’s privacy practices apply in addition to this policy for the client.
  • Federation / mesh matching may pair you with users on cooperating hubs. Video remains WebRTC between peers when possible; signaling may cross hubs.
page.privacy.intro: {brand} is a peer-to-peer video chat service. This page describes what we process, where it lives, how long we keep it, and what you can control.

page.privacy.langNote: If a translation differs from the English version, the English text controls.
page.privacy.lawBody: We may disclose information we hold (for example reports, friend codes, connection logs) when required by law, valid legal process, or to protect users and the Service from serious harm. We do not have a permanent archive of your live video streams to hand over.
page.privacy.local: Your browser may store preferences (language, theme, devices, friend history, identity) in localStorage and a device crypto key in IndexedDB (when available). You can export a profile file (Settings → About → Export) to move the same identity to another browser or device; friends lists for that identity are stored on the match hub. You can clear local data from Settings → Clear local data. Treat export files like passwords — anyone with the file may claim that identity on a hub.
page.privacy.media1: Call media (camera/microphone) is exchanged directly between browsers (WebRTC, encrypted with DTLS/SRTP) when the network allows a direct path. We do not operate a media server that stores or rebroadcasts your video/audio streams.
page.privacy.media2: If a direct connection fails, media may be relayed through a TURN server (still encrypted on the media path). Prefer a direct path when the UI shows “Direct P2P”. Relay operators may see connection metadata needed to forward packets; they are not meant to archive your call content.
page.privacy.media3: Your partner can always screenshot or record what they see. Use Block and Report if needed. Self-hide (blur) only changes what you send; it is not encryption against a determined partner.
page.privacy.reports: If you report a user, we store the report (reporter id, target id, reason, time, and related session context) to fight abuse. Multiple independent reports may temporarily or permanently restrict matchmaking for the reported identity on this hub. Optional on-device AI may send an assisted report signal without uploading video to us. See Safety.
page.privacy.retentionBody:
• Signaling / live session data — kept only as long as needed to run the match and short operational logs.
  • Reports & enforcement — kept long enough to investigate abuse and apply bans; not a public archive.
  • Friends / blocks / friend DMs — kept while the relationship or ban is active on that hub, or until purged under that hub’s operations.
  • Local browser data — until you clear it or uninstall/clear site data.
  • Media streams — we do not keep a permanent video library of your calls. Partners or network middleboxes outside our control may still capture what they see.
  • Deletion requests — clear local data in Settings; email privacy@ruletka.vip with your friend code / approximate times if you need hub-side friend or report records reviewed. We may not be able to erase every log copy or data a partner already received.
page.privacy.rightsBody:
• Camera & mic — controlled by your browser permissions; you can revoke them anytime.
  • Hide / blur — optional self-hide so partners see black or blurred content while your preview stays on.
  • Block & Report — reduce rematches and flag abuse.
  • Export / clear local data — Settings → About / Clear local data.
  • Contact — privacy questions: privacy@ruletka.vip.
  • Because there is no classic account login, “access my data” often means what is on your device plus what you can identify to support (friend code, approximate dates).
page.privacy.securityBody:
• Live client traffic uses encrypted transport (HTTPS/WSS). WebRTC media uses DTLS/SRTP on the media path when the browser establishes it.
  • We take reasonable care to protect hub systems, but no online service is perfectly secure. You use random video chat at your own risk.
  • Do not share secrets, passwords, financial data, or anything you would not show a stranger.
page.privacy.signal: To match strangers and connect calls, our bridge may process temporary connection data (WebSocket session ids, display names you choose, room codes, friend codes, WebRTC offers/answers/ICE, and short-lived chat for the session). This is required for the service to work. We minimize long-term retention of raw signaling payloads after the session ends.
page.privacy.summaryHtml:
We do

  • Match you and pass WebRTC signaling so a call can start
  • Store reports and friend data on the hub you use (for safety and friends features)
  • Keep preferences and identity in your browser (and optional export file)
  • Load analytics only if the operator configures measurement ids

We don’t

  • Store or rebroadcast your camera/mic stream as a permanent archive
  • Require a classic email/password account
  • Sell your video feed to advertisers
  • Guarantee that partners won’t screenshot or record what they see
page.privacy.title: Privacy policy — {brand}
page.safety.aiP1: Optional auto-skip explicit video runs in your browser (nsfwjs). Frames never leave your device for that model. If it fires, the partner is blurred, blocked, and you search again. The hub also receives an AI-assisted report signal so repeated offenders across users can be restricted — with a higher threshold than pure human “explicit” reports to limit false positives.
page.safety.hTools: What you can do in a call
page.safety.idP: There is no classic login. Each browser starts as its own identity until you Settings → About → Export / Import profile. Friends live on the hub under your user id — import restores that id so friends return on this hub.
page.safety.intro: Video is peer-to-peer between browsers. We cannot “watch” every call on a central media server — and we don’t claim that. Safety is a mix of your tools, community reports, and automatic hub rules.
page.safety.liBlock: Block — never match this identity again on this hub.
page.safety.liBlur: Blur — new strangers start blurred for 2 seconds so you can hit Next, then unblur automatically. Settings → Safety can keep them blurred until you unblur.
page.safety.liNext: Next — leave this partner and search again.
page.safety.liReport: Report — dock button or click the partner video → Report. Pick a reason; we block them and skip for you immediately. Multiple independent reports can auto-restrict their matchmaking.
page.safety.liStart: Start — begin searching from the center of the partner window (also after Stop).
page.safety.liStop: Stop — leave the queue and stay idle (keyboard S). No pressure to keep searching.
page.safety.multiNote: Reporters are rate-limited so mass false reports are harder. This is not a police service and not perfect — use Block for yourself, and Report to protect others.
page.safety.multiP: Reports are stored on this hub. Independent users reporting the same identity can trigger a temporary matchmaking ban (they can’t enter the stranger queue). Thresholds by reason:
page.safety.opsP: Optional admin UI at /admin.html (token required) lists reports and bans. Optional webhook ROULETTE_MOD_WEBHOOK_URL can notify you when auto-ban fires (Telegram, Slack, or Discord HTTPS URL). Federation tokens stay private. See the open-source docs/OPS.md operator guide.
page.safety.partnersP: Anyone you video with can screenshot or record what they see. Do not show documents, faces of minors, or secrets you wouldn’t share in public. Prefer a private room or friends only when you need more control.
page.safety.title: Safety on {brand} — report, block, AI skip

page.terms.idBody:
• No classic account required. The client may create a local identity (for example a user id and friend code) stored in your browser.
  • You may set a display name, optional avatar, and cosmetic flag. These are shown to partners and friends. Do not use names that violate §3.
  • Friends are mutual and stored on the hub instance you use so online status and DMs can work. Friend requests require accept.
  • Match chat may be kept on your device after a call ends. Friend messages may be stored on the hub for delivery when the other person is offline.
  • Exporting a profile may move your identity key between devices; clearing local data removes local copies on that device. Friends and some server-side records may remain on the hub until removed or purged under our practices.
  • See the Privacy policy for what is processed where.

page.terms.safeBody:
• You can use Next, Stop, Block, Report, partner mute/blur, and self-hide where available.
  • Reports may be stored and reviewed by automated systems and/or operators. Multiple independent reports may temporarily or permanently restrict matchmaking for an identity on a hub.
  • Optional on-device filters may skip or flag explicit material; they are imperfect and do not replace your judgment.
  • You are responsible for who you talk to. A stranger can still screenshot, record, or misuse what they see. Do not share secrets, passwords, financial data, or anything you would not show a stranger in public.
  • In an emergency, contact local emergency services. We are not a crisis line.
page.terms.svcBody:
• Matchmaking & signaling — a hub (bridge) helps pair users and exchange WebRTC offers/answers/ICE and text chat for the session.
  • Video & audio — when the network allows, media is peer-to-peer WebRTC (encrypted on the media path). We do not run a permanent video recording store for calls.
  • TURN / relay — if a direct path fails, encrypted media may pass through a relay. Quality and availability depend on your network and capacity.
  • Optional features — rooms, friends, party browse, messages, device settings, themes, and similar tools as shown in the client.

The Service is offered for personal, non-commercial use unless we agree otherwise in writing. Features may change, break, or be limited without notice. There is no guarantee of continuous uptime, match availability, or a successful call.

page.terms.thirdBody:

  • If you connect to a non–ruletka.vip hub, that operator’s terms and privacy practices apply in addition to any local client EULA.
  • Federation / mesh matching may connect you with users on cooperating hubs. Video remains WebRTC between peers when possible; signaling may cross hubs.
  • Third-party links, wallets, app stores, or tunnels are not controlled by us. Use them at your own risk.

page.terms.useBody:

  • Harass, threaten, stalk, dox, blackmail, or abuse others.
  • Share hate speech, violent threats, or content that promotes illegal activity.
  • Transmit illegal content (including CSAM, non-consensual intimate imagery, fraud materials, or content that infringes others’ rights).
  • Spam, scam, phish, or run deceptive schemes (crypto “giveaways”, fake support, etc.).
  • Disrupt the Service: flood matchmaking, abuse APIs, attack infrastructure, probe other users’ devices, or distribute malware.
  • Use bots, scripts, or automation to mass-match, mass-message, or scrape users without our prior written permission.
  • Circumvent bans, blocks, rate limits, or safety systems (including creating identities solely to evade enforcement).
  • Impersonate others in a misleading way for harm or fraud.
  • Record, stream, or publish another person’s video/audio without their consent where that is illegal or prohibited by these Terms.

More practical rules for everyday chat are in the Community guidelines and Safety pages. If those conflict with these Terms, these Terms control for legal purposes.
